newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling weaker vs dlr on good demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling weaker vs dlr on good demand.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling weakened marginally against the dollar on Thursday on increased dollar buying interest from corporate importers and the Central Bank of Kenya, commercial bank dealers said.
The central bank posted a mean shilling average of 55.34 against the dollar from 55.33 on Wednesday, while on the sterling pound, it was posted at 91.04 unchanged.

Some dealers said good volumes of inflows from export sales continued to stream in causing the shilling to firm, but matching demand from importers and the central bank held the shilling range-bound within the 55.30/40 region.
"The shilling weakened marginally when the central bank came in late on Wednesday afternoon buying dollars at the 55.35 levels," one dealer said.
Another dealer said the interbank market was fairly active in cross-currency trading.
Dealers expect the shilling to trade within the 55.30/40 region till the week-end in the absence of any significant factors.

The money market was a still liquid as players piled money in anticipation of tigter rates next week. The overnight rates were quoted as high as 12 percent from between five and ten percent levels on Wednesday.
